The affected units were sold nationwide through direct sales and heating and cooling dealers from May 2015 through January 2023. The case marks the first-ever corporate criminal enforcement action brought under the Consumer Product Safety Act (CPSA). This growth was notably influenced by shifts in product demand, with a 7% increase in the sales of heat pumps and a 9% rise in ductless HVAC systems. These standards are projected to save American consumers approximately $1.5 billion annually on their utility bills and are expected to reduce carbon dioxide emissions by 106 million metric tons over 30 years. The new requirements for portable air cleaners will take effect in 2024, while the standards for room air conditioners will become effective on May 26, 2026.

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> The National Electrical Contractors Association (NECA) will hold its 2025 annual convention and trade show in Chicago, Illinois, from September 12-15, 2025. [2, 3, 7] Philadelphia was the location for the 2023 convention. [9] The NECA Show is the premier event for the $225 billion electrical construction industry, bringing together leaders to explore emerging trends in power, light, and communication technology. [2, 4] The event, held at McCormick Place, will feature a trade show with over 300 exhibitors showcasing new products and solutions, alongside a comprehensive educational program with workshops on technology, construction solutions, and leadership. [2, 4, 5] <2> A market research report from Expert Market Research indicates that the United States air conditioners (AC) market is expected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5.60% during the forecast period of 2025 to 2034. The market was valued at approximately USD 23.90 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach USD 41.21 billion by 2034. This growth is driven by several factors, including the increasing need for air conditioning in both residential and commercial sectors due to rising temperatures associated with climate change. Key drivers identified are the escalating development of energy-efficient and sustainable air conditioners and the growing consumer trend of installing smart, connected devices that allow for control via smartphones and provide data on energy consumption and performance. Conflictingly, another report from the same source, but with a different publication date, suggests the market will grow at the same CAGR of 5.6% but within a 2024-2032 timeframe, reaching a value of USD 37.28 billion. <3> For 2024, experts in the HVAC industry correctly anticipated several key trends, emphasizing a significant move towards technological and environmental advancements. There is a greater focus on smart HVAC systems with IoT integration, which provide homeowners and businesses with enhanced control, efficiency, and comfort. [1, 4] In line with a growing environmental consciousness, the integration of renewable energy sources is also a major trend, with solar and geothermal-powered systems gaining popularity due to their low energy consumption. [2, 5, 6] Furthermore, indoor air quality has become a priority, leading to the incorporation of advanced purification features in air conditioning systems; technologies such as HEPA filters, UV-C lights, air scrubbers, and other integrated purifiers are becoming standard to effectively remove airborne particles and allergens. [3, 7] A critical regulatory and environmental shift is the ongoing transition to low-Global Warming Potential (GWP) refrigerants, with eco-friendly options like R-32 and R-454B gaining traction as the industry phases out older substances. [8, 9] This transition includes new pricing structures for reclaimed refrigerants introduced in 2024. [9] <4> In January 2024, the Air-Conditioning, Heating, and Refrigeration Institute (AHRI) reported that combined U.S. shipments of central air conditioners and air-source heat pumps amounted to 479,374 units. This figure represents a 21.3% decrease from the 609,156 units shipped in January 2023. Specifically, shipments of central air conditioners saw a 24.3% decline to 248,035 units, while air-source heat pump shipments fell by 17.9% to 231,339 units. The data, which tracks when a unit's ownership is transferred, is for shipments to customers within the United States only. AHRI notes that while some use shipments and sales interchangeably, they may not be the same. <5> LG Electronics presented its new DUALCOOL residential air conditioner at the Mostra Convegno Expocomfort (MCE) 2024 exhibition in Milan, Italy, which took place from March 12-15. The new model is engineered for the European market and features high energy efficiency, boasting an A+++ EU energy efficiency rating. Key technologies contributing to its efficiency include the DUAL Inverter Heat Pump Compressor™ and a kW Manager™ function, which allows users to monitor and set electricity usage targets via the ThinQ™ app. For enhanced user comfort, the air conditioner is equipped with a 'Soft Air' function that provides a gentle, indirect breeze. It also incorporates an innovative DUAL Vane™ system and a Human Detection Sensor, which work together to optimize airflow direction and intensity based on the presence and location of people in the room. <6> A report from the Air-Conditioning, Heating, and Refrigeration Institute (AHRI), published on February 16, 2024, revealed a significant decrease in U.S. shipments of central air conditioners and air-source heat pumps for December 2023 compared to December 2022. Combined shipments of these units totaled 435,589 in December 2023, a 29.3% decrease from the 616,201 units shipped in December 2022. Specifically, shipments of central air conditioners fell by 25.3% to 238,542 units, and air-source heat pump shipments declined by 33.7% to 197,047 units. For the entire calendar year of 2023, the combined shipments of both product categories experienced a 16.7% drop, down to 8,656,674 units from 10,388,054 in 2022. <7> At the 2024 AHR Expo held in Chicago from January 22-24, several companies introduced new technologies focused on higher efficiency and low-Global Warming Potential (GWP) refrigerants. Danfoss showcased its DSG compressor, which won an Innovation Award in the Cooling category and is designed for low-pressure, low-GWP refrigerants like R-1234ze. The company Ephoca won the top Product of the Year award for its Nextac PTAC unit, a next-generation system that uses R-32 refrigerant, features a twin rotary inverter compressor, and offers high efficiency and quiet operation. Carrier presented its range of sustainable solutions, including the compact AquaEdge 19MV water-cooled chiller, which uses a low-GWP refrigerant, and the AquaSnap 30RC air-cooled chiller with Greenspeed intelligence. Daikin highlighted its commitment to decarbonization with products using R-32 refrigerant, featuring its Trailblazer AGZ-F, one of the first R-32 air-cooled scroll chillers available in North America, and other heat pump systems. <8> At CES 2024, held from January 9-12 in Las Vegas, TCL showcased an expanded portfolio of products, including its latest air conditioning units. The company presented its TCL FreshIN series of air conditioners, which feature technologies for bringing in fresh air, high-efficiency purification, and energy savings. While much of the focus was on their split-unit FreshIN models, which are not window units, TCL did announce its first window air conditioner featuring the Matter protocol for smart home integration. A "nearly silent and highly energy-efficient" unit aligns with features promoted for other TCL air conditioners, such as the Q-Series window AC, which boasts ultra-quiet operation (down to 40dB) and up to 38% energy savings via an AI Inverter. TCL also highlighted its commitment to energy efficiency with AI algorithms designed to optimize performance and reduce consumption.

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Forest River, Inc. has recalled approximately 2,783 motorhomes from model years 2021-2025 due to a fire hazard. The affected vehicles are equipped with General Electric air conditioners containing a soft start device, part number ICM870-16A-BH5400, which can fail and overheat, increasing the risk of fire. According to an alert from GE Appliances, the soft start modules may have an unknown design or manufacturing defect. While a remedy is still under development, owners are advised to have the soft start device removed. Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed on November 26, 2024. The recall, identified by NHTSA Campaign Number 24V771 and Forest River number 51-1839, includes the following models: 2024 Ahara and Entrada; 2022-2025 FR3 and Georgetown; 2021-2023 Dynamax Isata; 2021-2025 Encore, Mirada, and Pursuit; 2025 Sportscoach, V-Cruise, V-Sport, and V-Tour; 2023 Sunseeker; and 2024-2025 V-RV. <2> The 2025 ASHRAE Winter Conference is scheduled to take place in Orlando, Florida, from February 8-12, 2025, at the Hilton Orlando. [1, 2, 4] The conference program will cover a wide range of topics, with a technical program featuring over 100 sessions across nine tracks. [1, 5, 8] Key focus areas include HVAC/R fundamentals, the development of new HVAC/R systems and equipment, evolving refrigerant regulations, and pathways to building decarbonization. [8, 10] Additionally, the program will delve into subjects such as indoor environmental quality (IEQ), energy storage and grid resiliency, artificial intelligence in building automation, and industrialized construction. [8, 10] Running concurrently with the conference is the AHR Expo, which will showcase new technologies and products from over 1,600 exhibitors. [1] The technical program's availability was announced in late 2024. [9, 10] <3> The 2025 ASHRAE Annual Conference, a significant event for professionals in the heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and refrigeration (HVACR) industry, is scheduled to be held in Phoenix, Arizona, from June 21 to June 25, 2025. The conference will take place at the Sheraton Phoenix Downtown and the Phoenix Convention Center. The event serves as a platform for discussing the latest research and technological advancements in the field. The call for abstracts for the conference was announced on September 19, 2024, with various submission deadlines for different types of papers. The technical program will feature over 80 sessions across eight tracks, covering topics such as decarbonization, heat pumps, refrigerants, thermal energy storage, industrial ventilation, and workforce development. The conference will also include professional development courses, technical tours, and networking opportunities. <4> A market analysis by Spherical Insights indicates that the United States Air Conditioner Market was valued at USD 23.88 billion in 2023. The report, published in July 2024, forecasts a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5.59% from 2023 to 2033, with the market size expected to reach USD 41.15 billion by 2033. The growth is attributed to the widespread use of air conditioners in residential, commercial, and industrial sectors, driven by rising temperatures due to climate change and the increasing demand for affordable and energy-efficient units. <5> On June 13, 2024, Daikin Comfort Technologies Manufacturing announced a recall of approximately 12,100 Amana, Daikin, and Goodman branded packaged air conditioners and heat pumps due to a fire hazard. [1, 3, 5] The recall, issued in conjunction with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, states that the unit's serial plate can have incorrect electrical ratings, potentially leading to the use of improper wiring and posing a fire risk. [1, 5] The affected units, sold by independent dealers nationwide between January and March 2024 for $4,500 to $7,500, are either gray or green. [4, 6] No incidents or injuries have been reported. [3, 4] Consumers are advised not to open the unit's electrical panel and to contact Daikin for a free inspection and repair. [1, 5] <6> The National Electrical Contractors Association (NECA) will hold its 2025 annual convention and trade show in Chicago, Illinois, from September 12-15, 2025. [2, 3, 7] Philadelphia was the location for the 2023 convention. [9] The NECA Show is the premier event for the $225 billion electrical construction industry, bringing together leaders to explore emerging trends in power, light, and communication technology. [2, 4] The event, held at McCormick Place, will feature a trade show with over 300 exhibitors showcasing new products and solutions, alongside a comprehensive educational program with workshops on technology, construction solutions, and leadership. [2, 4, 5] <7> RefriAméricas is a prominent international conference and expo for the HVACR (Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning, and Refrigeration) industry focused on Latin America and the Caribbean. [4] The 2024 edition, which marked the event's 20th anniversary, took place in Miami, Florida, at the Miami Airport Convention Center from July 24-25, 2024. [3, 4, 6] The event featured over 100 exhibitors showcasing the latest technologies, an academic congress with sessions in both Spanish and English, and attracted thousands of industry professionals. [3, 6, 7] A virtual pre-congress was also held on June 25, 2024, ahead of the main event. [11] A past edition was held in Puerto Rico, but the 2024 event took place in Miami. [10] <8> A market research report from Expert Market Research indicates that the United States air conditioners (AC) market is expected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5.60% during the forecast period of 2025 to 2034. The market was valued at approximately USD 23.90 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach USD 41.21 billion by 2034. This growth is driven by several factors, including the increasing need for air conditioning in both residential and commercial sectors due to rising temperatures associated with climate change. Key drivers identified are the escalating development of energy-efficient and sustainable air conditioners and the growing consumer trend of installing smart, connected devices that allow for control via smartphones and provide data on energy consumption and performance. Conflictingly, another report from the same source, but with a different publication date, suggests the market will grow at the same CAGR of 5.6% but within a 2024-2032 timeframe, reaching a value of USD 37.28 billion. <9> For 2024, experts in the HVAC industry correctly anticipated several key trends, emphasizing a significant move towards technological and environmental advancements. There is a greater focus on smart HVAC systems with IoT integration, which provide homeowners and businesses with enhanced control, efficiency, and comfort. [1, 4] In line with a growing environmental consciousness, the integration of renewable energy sources is also a major trend, with solar and geothermal-powered systems gaining popularity due to their low energy consumption. [2, 5, 6] Furthermore, indoor air quality has become a priority, leading to the incorporation of advanced purification features in air conditioning systems; technologies such as HEPA filters, UV-C lights, air scrubbers, and other integrated purifiers are becoming standard to effectively remove airborne particles and allergens. [3, 7] A critical regulatory and environmental shift is the ongoing transition to low-Global Warming Potential (GWP) refrigerants, with eco-friendly options like R-32 and R-454B gaining traction as the industry phases out older substances. [8, 9] This transition includes new pricing structures for reclaimed refrigerants introduced in 2024. [9] <10> In January 2024, the Air-Conditioning, Heating, and Refrigeration Institute (AHRI) reported that combined U.S. shipments of central air conditioners and air-source heat pumps amounted to 479,374 units. This figure represents a 21.3% decrease from the 609,156 units shipped in January 2023. Specifically, shipments of central air conditioners saw a 24.3% decline to 248,035 units, while air-source heat pump shipments fell by 17.9% to 231,339 units. The data, which tracks when a unit's ownership is transferred, is for shipments to customers within the United States only. AHRI notes that while some use shipments and sales interchangeably, they may not be the same.

This growth is primarily driven by increasing consumer demand for energy-efficient and sustainable heating and cooling solutions. Factors influencing this trend include a heightened focus on minimizing environmental impact and the availability of federal and state incentives, such as tax credits and rebates, which encourage the adoption of eco-friendly HVAC systems. The market is also seeing a surge in technologies like smart thermostats and IoT-integrated systems that enhance energy efficiency and user comfort. Other market analyses present different valuations; one report suggests the market was valued at USD 16.43 billion in 2023 and will reach USD 19.88 billion by 2029, while another values the broader U.S. HVAC systems market at USD 29.89 billion in 2024 with a projected growth to USD 54.02 billion by 2033. Government initiatives, including the Inflation Reduction Act, are noted as a significant driver across multiple reports for incentivizing the shift to more efficient systems. <2> Lifestory Research has named Trane as America's Most Trusted® HVAC brand for the 11th consecutive year in its 2025 study. This recognition is based on a nationwide survey of 8,856 consumers conducted between January and December 2024. Trane achieved the highest Net Trust Quotient Score of 113.4 among the most recognized HVAC brands. The study, active for over a decade, measures consumer trust based on their experiences and opinions to identify the most trusted brands in various product categories, with new results released each January. <3> Goodman Group has introduced Norges Bank Investment Management (NBIM) as the new capital partner in its Goodman North American Partnership (GNAP). NBIM, which manages Norway's sovereign wealth fund, acquired the 45% interest previously held by the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (CPP Investments) for $1.07 billion. The transaction, which valued the total GNAP portfolio at approximately $3.3 billion, closed on January 1, 2025. Goodman Group will retain its 55% majority stake and continue to serve as the asset manager for the partnership. The GNAP platform is focused on investing in and developing high-quality logistics and industrial properties in key North American markets, including Southern California, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania. As part of the restructuring, Goodman Group also acquired a portfolio of value-add and development properties from GNAP. CPP Investments, which co-founded GNAP with Goodman in 2012, stated the sale allows them to realize strong returns and redeploy capital into new opportunities. <4> Build Expo USA hosts a series of premier regional trade shows for the construction and design industries, providing a platform for professionals, including those in the HVAC sector, to network, attend accredited classes, and discover new products and innovations. In 2025, the expo will hold an event in Tampa, Florida, from January 22-23 at the Tampa Convention Center. Another event is scheduled for Austin, Texas, from March 19-20 at the Palmer Events Center. <5> Forest River, Inc. has recalled approximately 2,783 motorhomes from model years 2021-2025 due to a fire hazard. The affected vehicles are equipped with General Electric air conditioners containing a soft start device, part number ICM870-16A-BH5400, which can fail and overheat, increasing the risk of fire. According to an alert from GE Appliances, the soft start modules may have an unknown design or manufacturing defect. While a remedy is still under development, owners are advised to have the soft start device removed. Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed on November 26, 2024. The recall, identified by NHTSA Campaign Number 24V771 and Forest River number 51-1839, includes the following models: 2024 Ahara and Entrada; 2022-2025 FR3 and Georgetown; 2021-2023 Dynamax Isata; 2021-2025 Encore, Mirada, and Pursuit; 2025 Sportscoach, V-Cruise, V-Sport, and V-Tour; 2023 Sunseeker; and 2024-2025 V-RV. <6> The 2025 ASHRAE Winter Conference is scheduled to take place in Orlando, Florida, from February 8-12, 2025, at the Hilton Orlando. [1, 2, 4] The conference program will cover a wide range of topics, with a technical program featuring over 100 sessions across nine tracks. [1, 5, 8] Key focus areas include HVAC/R fundamentals, the development of new HVAC/R systems and equipment, evolving refrigerant regulations, and pathways to building decarbonization. [8, 10] Additionally, the program will delve into subjects such as indoor environmental quality (IEQ), energy storage and grid resiliency, artificial intelligence in building automation, and industrialized construction. [8, 10] Running concurrently with the conference is the AHR Expo, which will showcase new technologies and products from over 1,600 exhibitors. [1] The technical program's availability was announced in late 2024. [9, 10] <7> The 2025 ASHRAE Annual Conference, a significant event for professionals in the heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and refrigeration (HVACR) industry, is scheduled to be held in Phoenix, Arizona, from June 21 to June 25, 2025. The conference will take place at the Sheraton Phoenix Downtown and the Phoenix Convention Center. The event serves as a platform for discussing the latest research and technological advancements in the field. The call for abstracts for the conference was announced on September 19, 2024, with various submission deadlines for different types of papers. The technical program will feature over 80 sessions across eight tracks, covering topics such as decarbonization, heat pumps, refrigerants, thermal energy storage, industrial ventilation, and workforce development. The conference will also include professional development courses, technical tours, and networking opportunities. <8> A market analysis by Spherical Insights indicates that the United States Air Conditioner Market was valued at USD 23.88 billion in 2023. The report, published in July 2024, forecasts a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5.59% from 2023 to 2033, with the market size expected to reach USD 41.15 billion by 2033. The growth is attributed to the widespread use of air conditioners in residential, commercial, and industrial sectors, driven by rising temperatures due to climate change and the increasing demand for affordable and energy-efficient units. <9> On June 13, 2024, Daikin Comfort Technologies Manufacturing announced a recall of approximately 12,100 Amana, Daikin, and Goodman branded packaged air conditioners and heat pumps due to a fire hazard. [1, 3, 5] The recall, issued in conjunction with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, states that the unit's serial plate can have incorrect electrical ratings, potentially leading to the use of improper wiring and posing a fire risk. [1, 5] The affected units, sold by independent dealers nationwide between January and March 2024 for $4,500 to $7,500, are either gray or green. [4, 6] No incidents or injuries have been reported. [3, 4] Consumers are advised not to open the unit's electrical panel and to contact Daikin for a free inspection and repair. [1, 5] <10> The National Electrical Contractors Association (NECA) will hold its 2025 annual convention and trade show in Chicago, Illinois, from September 12-15, 2025. [2, 3, 7] Philadelphia was the location for the 2023 convention. [9] The NECA Show is the premier event for the $225 billion electrical construction industry, bringing together leaders to explore emerging trends in power, light, and communication technology. [2, 4] The event, held at McCormick Place, will feature a trade show with over 300 exhibitors showcasing new products and solutions, alongside a comprehensive educational program with workshops on technology, construction solutions, and leadership. [2, 4, 5]
